items.title: Kubernetes v1.37: Native Histograms Graduates to Beta
items.blurb: I'm excited to announce that native histogram support for Kubernetes metrics is graduating to Beta and is enabled by default in Kubernetes v1.37!

items.title: Kubernetes v1.37: Scheduler Preemption for In-Place Pod Resize (Alpha)
items.blurb: In Kubernetes, resource allocation has historically been a static decision made during a Pod's initial scheduling and placement.

items.title: Kubernetes v1.37: Introducing Node Lifecycle Conditions
items.blurb: Kubernetes has many ways to describe what is happening on a Node. Readiness, taints, Pod state, labels, annotations, and provider-specific APIs each expose part of the picture.

items.title: Kubernetes v1.37: Advancing Workload-Aware Scheduling
items.blurb: AI/ML and complex batch workloads continue to push the boundaries of Kubernetes scheduling.

items.title: Presentation: How To Run on Three Clouds at Once, and When Not To
items.blurb: Ross McFarlane and Kevin Holditch discuss Form3's evolution from a single-cloud setup to a triple active multi-cloud architecture.

items.title: Presentation: Fixing the AI Infra Scale Problem by Stuffing 1M Sandboxes in a Single Server
items.blurb: Felipe Huici explains how Unikraft achieves millisecond cold boots, stateful scale-to-zero, and extreme density for sandboxing AI workloads.

items.title: Kubernetes Promotes KYAML as a Safer, More Consistent Way to Work with Manifests
items.blurb: Kubernetes is encouraging developers to take a closer look at KYAML, a stricter dialect of YAML designed to make Kubernetes configuration more explicit, predictable, and less prone to common YAML errors. By Craig Risi
